Services.title: The boring stuff, done properly.
Services.intro: Month-end, tax deadlines, reconciliations, forecasts. The things that never feel urgent until they very much are.

Process.title: No jargon. No surprises. Slightly obsessive.
Process.stepOneText: Thirty minutes, free. You tell me what hurts. I tell you honestly whether I can help.
Process.stepTwoText: I go through what you have and tell you what is off, in plain language, with a fix for each point.
Process.stepThreeText: A monthly close, a reporting calendar and tax deadlines locked in. You always know what happens when.
Process.stepFourText: Numbers arrive on time and make sense. I carry on being a little bit manic so you do not have to be.

About.title: Yes, Manic is my real surname.
About.paragraphOne: Everybody makes the joke, so I made it the brand. Behind the pun is a decade in finance and controlling: from general ledger and reconciliations to leading a finance team and steering costs across global functions of a multinational.
About.paragraphTwo: I have closed the books for entities in Europe, the US and Canada, built process automation for accounting teams, and filed VAT in three countries. By day I am a finance controller. Now I am bringing the same obsessiveness to a few smaller businesses who deserve it too.

DebtCapacityPage.metaTitle: Free debt repayment capacity calculator for small businesses
DebtCapacityPage.metaDescription: Test a 13-week debt repayment plan, calculate a safe weekly repayment ceiling, protect a minimum cash buffer and stress-test lower sales or higher costs.
DebtCapacityPage.keywords: debt repayment capacity calculator|business debt repayment calculator|13 week cash flow forecast|debt service capacity|cash flow debt analysis|small business debt planning|repayment capacity analysis
DebtCapacityPage.title: Can the business repay the debt without starving the bank account?
DebtCapacityPage.intro: Connect planned repayments to weekly operating cash, one-off commitments and a minimum safety buffer. Adjust the assumptions and see where the plan becomes uncomfortable before it becomes urgent.
DebtCapacityPage.howTextOne: The model starts with opening cash, weekly customer receipts and operating costs. It then deducts the planned weekly debt repayment and any one-off payment across a rolling 13-week view.
DebtCapacityPage.howTextTwo: The safe weekly ceiling is the highest estimated repayment that keeps every projected week above the minimum cash buffer you choose.
DebtCapacityPage.mattersTitle: Cash headroom matters more than a green ending balance
DebtCapacityPage.mattersText: A plan can finish positive and still become fragile in the middle. Focus on the lowest week, the buffer shortfall and how quickly the answer changes under stress.
DebtCapacityPage.disclaimer: This is an illustrative planning tool, not accounting, investment or lending advice. Actual capacity also depends on loan terms, interest, taxes, seasonality and collection risk.

BreakEvenPage.metaTitle: Free pricing, profit margin and break-even calculator
BreakEvenPage.metaDescription: Calculate contribution margin, break-even sales volume, target-profit volume and minimum selling price. Stress-test lower prices or higher variable costs for free.
BreakEvenPage.keywords: break even calculator|profit margin calculator|pricing calculator for small business|contribution margin calculator|target profit calculator|service business pricing calculator|break even sales volume
BreakEvenPage.title: How much must you sell before the work actually makes money?
BreakEvenPage.intro: Connect selling price, variable costs, monthly overhead and expected volume. The calculator shows contribution margin, break-even sales, target-profit requirements and the minimum price your plan needs.
BreakEvenPage.howTextOne: Every sale first covers its own variable cost. What remains is contribution: the amount available to cover monthly fixed costs and, only after that, profit.
BreakEvenPage.howTextTwo: Break-even volume divides fixed costs by contribution per sale. Target-profit volume adds the desired profit before performing the same calculation.
BreakEvenPage.useTitle: Use it for decisions, not decoration
BreakEvenPage.useText: Test a price increase, supplier-cost change, new monthly expense or realistic sales target. If a small assumption change destroys the margin, the plan needs more room.
BreakEvenPage.disclaimer: This is an illustrative planning calculator. It excludes VAT, income tax, financing, capacity limits, customer mix and timing differences unless you include them in your inputs.

BreakEvenTool.title: Pricing and break-even calculator

scenarioNote.base: The current price, costs and expected monthly sales volume.
scenarioNote.priceDrop: Selling price is reduced by 5% to show how quickly a discount changes the required volume.
scenarioNote.costRise: Variable cost is increased by 10% to test supplier, contractor or delivery-cost pressure.

BreakEvenTool.chartIntro: The crossing point is break-even. Horizontal scale: {sale}.
BreakEvenTool.chartLabel: Chart comparing revenue and total costs. Break-even occurs at {breakEven} {sale}.
BreakEvenTool.minimumPriceNote: Price needed at the expected volume to cover costs and target profit.

verdict.invalid: Variable cost is equal to or above the selling price. Each sale loses money before fixed costs, so break-even is impossible.
verdict.loss: At the expected volume, the plan loses {profit}. Break-even starts at approximately {units} sales.
verdict.tight: The plan is profitable, but the margin of safety is thin. Contribution is {contribution} per sale, so a small volume miss can remove the profit.
verdict.healthy: The expected volume is comfortably above break-even. Contribution is {contribution} per sale, leaving useful room before the plan turns negative.

BreakEvenTool.disclaimer: Amounts use your own currency. Results are illustrative and depend entirely on the costs and volume assumptions entered.

ThreeStatementPage.metaTitle: Free three-statement financial forecast for service businesses
ThreeStatementPage.metaDescription: Create a free connected P&L, balance sheet and indirect cash flow forecast. Adjust DSO, DPO, growth, margins, capex and debt, then export an Excel-compatible workbook.
ThreeStatementPage.keywords: free three statement financial model|three statement forecast tool|P&L balance sheet cash flow forecast|DSO DPO forecast|service business financial model|Excel financial forecast template|SME cash flow model
ThreeStatementPage.title: See how profit turns into cash—and where it gets stuck.
ThreeStatementPage.intro: Enter a service business P&L, opening balance sheet and the assumptions that move cash. The model connects all three statements, updates instantly and gives you a workbook you can open in Excel.
ThreeStatementPage.howTextOne: Revenue and margin assumptions build the forecast P&L. DSO converts revenue into receivables, while DPO converts direct costs into payables. Capex, depreciation, debt repayment, interest and tax complete the operating picture.
ThreeStatementPage.howTextTwo: The indirect cash flow starts from net income, adjusts for non-cash depreciation and working-capital movements, then connects investing and financing cash flows back to the closing balance sheet.
ThreeStatementPage.limitsText: This first tool is designed for service businesses. It intentionally excludes inventory and DIO, complex debt facilities, dividends, deferred tax, acquisitions and detailed fixed-asset registers.
ThreeStatementPage.disclaimer: The result is an illustrative planning model, not accounting, tax, investment or lending advice. Review material decisions with a qualified professional who understands your business and jurisdiction.

ThreeStatementTool.historicalPnlNote: Use the latest normal trading year, before forecast growth.
ThreeStatementTool.openingBalanceNote: Enter balances at the date immediately before the forecast starts.
ThreeStatementTool.forecastDriversNote: The assumptions that connect profit, working capital, debt and cash.
ThreeStatementTool.serviceNote: Service-business model: inventory is excluded, so DIO is not required. Opening equity is calculated automatically as the balancing amount.
ThreeStatementTool.chartLabel: Forecast chart comparing revenue and ending cash by period.
ThreeStatementTool.privacyNote: All calculations and the workbook export run locally in your browser. The financial inputs are not sent to Manic Accounting.
